runs.name: AECOM; NYSE ACM, SEC CIK 0000868857, formerly AECOM Technology Corp to 2015; professional infrastructure consulting, design, construction and program management in three segments, Americas, International and AECOM Capital; Management Services and the self-perform at-risk construction businesses sold in fiscal 2020 and carried as discontinued; no rival named in the 10-K, Jacobs and Tetra Tech read as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: Price **$58.94** a share (close of 2026-10-16, Yahoo Finance; aggregator, flagged; $131.00 a year earlier). Shares **128,696,425** common, one class (10-Q Q3 fiscal 2026 cover, `0000868857-26-000021`; 128,695,633 issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30, repurchased shares retired, no treasury line). Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury 30-year par yield, 2026-10-15). Documents read: 10-K fiscal 2025 (`0000868857-25-000013`), 10-Ks fiscal 2024, 2022 and 2020, the three fiscal 2026 10-Qs, the proxy filed 2026-01-20 (`0000868857-26-000006`), the earnings 8-Ks of 2025-11-18 to 2026-08-10 and the revolving credit agreement 8-K of 2026-06-11. The brief's two stated departures: lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7 (the competition text, the contract mix and at-risk work, cash against reported earnings, the business that changed form, the AI risk factor), and the competitors the 10-K names; it names none, so Jacobs and Tetra Tech were read as a CONVENTION of the run (each names AECOM in its own 10-K), WSP, Stantec, Arcadis and the other non-10-K filers flagged. **Q1 IN**: fee-based design and program management billed on "our employees' time", about 53% of revenue subcontractor cost passed through, 38% cost-reimbursable, 37% guaranteed maximum price, 25% fixed price; the AI risk carried to Q2. **Q2 OUT**: the filer's own Item 1 and 1A say its services "provide limited barriers against new competitors" (Tetra Tech's 10-K the same words; Jacobs: no company dominates, 23 competitors named, Accenture and McKinsey among them); cost-plus fees negotiated with clients who list price among their tests; the margin gains since fiscal 2020 explained by the filer as restructuring, offshore centers, exits and mix, cost gains the rivals made too; the deciding part Americas, about 82% of three-year segment earnings. 2016 to 2025 averages: operating margin AECOM 3.4%, Jacobs 4.9%, Tetra Tech 7.6%; operating income on equity plus net debt 13.3%, 10.5%, 20.8%. Q3 to Q12 not reached. **COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE**: owner cash fiscal 2021 to 2025 mean $532.6M equity-only, $640.4M all-equity, flat to falling ($696.4M to $619.9M all-equity while operating income rose $629.6M to $1,026.5M), the twelve months to 2026-07-03 about $78.5M equity-only on two Construction Management projects; base $594.1M after acquisitions, the no-growth case the top and -2.87% a year the bottom, net debt $1,732.3M; value range **$54.22 to $71.56** a share all-equity ($69.60 to $80.68 equity-only) against $58.94, no case earns the floor (the no-growth case 6.38%); fair **$28.68 all-equity** ($40.33 equity-only); not armed, the box is OUT at Q2. Capital spending assumed all maintenance, a disclosed guess. Balance sheets 2016 to mid-2026: equity below goodwill every year-end, tangible equity always negative; retained earnings $948M (2018) to a deficit of $1,602M (June 2026) after $2.6B of buybacks fiscal 2021 to 2025; debt $4.1B to $2.1B on the 2020 sale proceeds, back to $2.75B principal; claims in contract assets about $160M to $620M at June 2026; receivables sold $349M. Facts after the stop, recorded not judged: a $336.8M fiscal 2026 loss on a project bid in 2019; buybacks at prices above $80 against a computed top of $71.56; adjusted figures in every release and guidance excluding the charge. Contamination declared by the analyst: a file-name listing of `Test Runs/` filtered for ACM or AECOM that returned another company's ACMR files (not opened, confessed in the self-audit as a breach of the rule's letter), the VSEC commit subjects and a memory index line naming no company; none used. Commits ea6d12cf (template), bc99b023 (Step 0 and Q1), 4aa0380b (Q2), efb554c2 (computation, box, close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` 45 distinct ids, PASS; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py` 58 id occurrences, no missing id, no E-id, four flags all verified as the checker reading a neighbouring id's quote (L2014-005, M2012-065, M2012-108) or the filer's quoted words: **no slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) whether a future technology threat the filer names belongs at Q1 (M1998-008 could close it TOO HARD) or at Q2; (2) which capital the ordinary-returns test means for a business with no tangible capital; (3) payments on businesses sold before the window; (4) a window that ends just before a known loss; (5) whether the all-equity add-back uses interest paid or interest expense, which sets the sign of the growth rate. Could not get: a maintenance and growth split of capital spending, the trailing finance-lease line, the non-10-K rivals, an organic owner-cash rate.
runs.narr: OUT at Q2 after Q1 IN (AECOM; infrastructure consulting, design and program management, Americas, International and AECOM Capital; the at-risk construction and Management Services businesses sold in fiscal 2020). The castle shown open on the filer's own 10-K, whose services "provide limited barriers against new competitors"; fees negotiated with price-testing clients in a field no firm dominates; the margin gains since 2020 cost gains the rivals made too; 2016 to 2025 operating margin 3.4% against Jacobs 4.9% and Tetra Tech 7.6%. Computation beneath the stop: owner cash flat while operating income rose, value $54.22 to $71.56 all-equity against $58.94, no case earns the floor, fair $28.68 ($40.33 equity-only), not armed. Facts recorded, not judged: a $336.8M fiscal 2026 project loss, claims assets near quadrupled since 2023, buybacks above $80. No citation slip. Framework gaps for the operator: a named technology threat at Q1 or Q2, ordinary returns with no tangible capital, payments on pre-window sales, a window ending before a known loss, interest paid or expense in the all-equity add-back.
